subcompetencies.name: Evaluation and Management of the Adult Orthopaedic Patient

level_1: Obtains a patient history, performs a physical examination and develops a differential diagnosis for patients across clinical settings
Formulates and executes a stabilization plan for emergent conditions

Leads an orthopaedic team in the management of patients with complex conditions (e.g., periprosthetic femur fractures in the setting of osteoporosis and medical comorbidities, complex elbow instability in the obese patient)
level_2: Manages patients with straightforward conditions, with direct supervision (e.g., fracture, arthritis)
Synthesizes a plan to manage healthy patients with straightforward conditions, including operative and non- operative options
Leads an orthopaedic team in the management of emergent conditions (e.g., polytrauma)
level_3: Recognizes and initiates work-up of emergent conditions (e.g. compartment syndrome, dysvascular limb, cauda equina syndrome)
Independently manages patients and adapts management plans for changing clinical situations
Develops a clinical pathway or guideline for the management of patients based on demonstrated clinical expertise
level_4: Orders and interprets diagnostic testing and consultations based on patient evaluation
Triages management of multiple emergent conditions
Leads a multidisciplinary team in the management of patients with complex conditions
level_5: Manages patients with straightforward conditions, with indirect supervision
Synthesizes a comprehensive plan to manage patients with complex conditions and comorbidities

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Describes basic health payment systems, including government, private, public, and uninsured care as well as different practice models
level_2: Describes how working within the health care system impacts patient care, including billing and coding
level_3: Analyzes how personal practice affects the system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
level_4: Uses shared decision- making in patient care, taking into consideration costs to the patient
level_5: Participates in advocacy activities for health policy

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence, and incorporate patient preferences and values in order to take care of a straightforward condition
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values in order to guide evidence-based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex conditions
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence to guide care, tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex conditions; and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Creates and implements a learning plan to optimize educational and professional development
level_2: Identifies the strengths, deficiencies and limitations in one’s knowledge and expertise
Actively seeks feedback and other input with adaptability, and humility
level_3: Demonstrates openness to feedback and other input in order to inform goals
Uses ongoing reflection, feedback, and other input to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and when necessary, improves it
level_4: Analyzes and reflects on the strengths, deficiencies and limitations in one’s knowledge and expertise to design a learning plan, with assistance
Role models consistently seeking feedback and other input with adaptability and humility
level_5: Responds to feedback and other input episodically, with adaptability, and humility
Coaches others on reflective practice

level_1: Identifies and describes inciting events for professionalism lapses
Integrates ethical principles and recognizes the need to seek help in complex situations
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying patient care (e.g., informed consent, surrogate decision making, advance directives, confidentiality, error disclosure, stewardship of limited resources, and related topics)
Recognizes situations that may promote professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in self and others
level_3: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in straightforward situations
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)
level_4: Applies ethical principles in straightforward situations and takes responsibility for lapses
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Reliably arrives to clinical activities on time and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion

level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities

level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in straightforward situations

level_4: Completes tasks and responsibilities without reminders
level_5: Prioritizes tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex situations

level_1: Recognizes the importance of addressing personal and professional well-being (e.g., physical and emotional health)
